#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Dataset integrity + schema check. Usage: python3 scripts/verify.py [--rebuild]"""
import hashlib, json, os, sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DATA = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "entries.dat")
DIGEST = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", ".digest")

digest = hashlib.sha256(open(DATA, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
if "--rebuild" in sys.argv:
    open(DIGEST, "w").write(digest)
    print("digest rebuilt")
    sys.exit(0)
if not os.path.exists(DIGEST) or open(DIGEST).read().strip() != digest:
    sys.exit("FAIL: digest mismatch (data/.digest does not match data/entries.dat)")
n = 0
for i, line in enumerate(open(DATA, encoding="utf-8"), 1):
    if not line.strip():
        continue
    try:
        e = json.loads(line)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        sys.exit("FAIL: line %d is not valid JSON" % i)
    if sorted(e) != ["prompt", "response"]:
        sys.exit("FAIL: line %d has wrong schema" % i)
    n += 1
print("ALL CHECKS PASSED (%d entries)" % n)
</tool_response>

Here is a 12-week kitchen renovation plan:

Weeks 1-2 (Planning + permits): Finalize your design and layout, get 3 contractor quotes, decide on materials/cabinets/appliances, submit any required building permits.

Weeks 3-4 (Demo + rough-ins): Clear out the old kitchen, remove cabinets and flooring, complete any electrical/plumbing rough-in work, frame any structural changes.

Weeks 5-7 (Installation phase): Install new cabinets, lay flooring, hang backsplash tiles, mount plumbing fixtures and lighting rough-ins.

Weeks 8-10 (Finishes + appliances): Install countertops, paint walls/trim, hook up appliances, install light fixtures and hardware.

Weeks 11-12 (Final touches + cleanup): Deep clean everything, fix punch-list items, final inspection if required, stage the space and enjoy your new kitchen.

Need a materials checklist for any particular week?

final_entries.prompt: We are launching a new fitness app and need a 6-week go-to-market marketing plan. Help me structure it.

final_entries.prompt: I need to prepare for a 5-day backpacking trip in the mountains. I have about 2 months to get ready. Give me a training and packing plan.
final_entries.response:
Here is an 8-week mountain backpacking prep plan:

Weeks 1-4 (Fitness base): Hike 2-3 times per week starting with 3-5 mile loops with a 15lb pack, add incline treadmill or stair sessions twice weekly, begin core and leg strength workouts (squats, lunges, planks) 3x per week.

Weeks 5-6 (Build endurance): One longer hike (8-10 miles) with your actual pack each weekend, practice setting up your tent at home, test all gear (stove, water filter, sleeping bag) to ensure everything works, gradually increase pack weight to full trip load.

Weeks 7-8 (Final prep): Do one overnight shakedown trip to verify your setup, finalize your itinerary and check trail conditions/weather, prep meals and freeze-dry if needed, create a pack checklist and verify every item fits.

Key principle: never bring untested gear into the backcountry.

Want a printable gear checklist tailored to your destination?

final_entries.prompt: I want to learn Rust from scratch to an intermediate level in about 3 months. I can dedicate roughly 10 hours per week. Plan this out for me.
final_entries.response:
Here is a 12-week Rust learning roadmap at ~10 hours/week:

Weeks 1-3 (Basics): Work through the official Rust Book (chapters 1-10) — focus on ownership, borrowing, lifetimes, and the type system. Complete all the exercises in each chapter, and write small CLI programs to practice.

Weeks 4-6 (Intermediate concepts): Study error handling (Result/Option), traits/generics, modules/crates, and the testing framework. Build 2 small projects (e.g., a CLI todo app and a simple web scraper) to apply these concepts.

Weeks 7-9 (Concurrency + ecosystem): Learn threads, channels, async/await with Tokio, and common crate patterns. Read through a few popular crate source files to see idiomatic Rust in action. Build a multi-threaded or async project.

Weeks 10-12 (Project + community): Contribute a small fix to an open-source Rust crate, complete the Rustlings exercises for weak areas, join r/learnrust and Rust Discord for feedback, and build one portfolio-worthy project that exercises everything.

Want me to suggest a specific portfolio project idea?
